target.scope: seed portfolio + derived jobs + active claims + terminal returns -> fallback/discovery transition

canonical_identity.problem: A fresh /wc can reach portfolio fallback after the normal frontier is saturated, but the current portfolio contract requires the worker to inspect seed jobs, derived jobs, claims and returns without requiring one durable machine-auditable receipt that explains why each higher-priority portfolio candidate was skipped and why allocation legitimately crossed into discovery. During this canary all nine non-terminal seed jobs had active claim directories, the Live seed had a terminal DONE return, and the derived root was absent; proving the transition currently requires reconstructing several repository reads by hand.
acceptance: Given PORTFOLIO.json plus current derived jobs, claims and returns, a deterministic allocator/auditor emits ordered candidates and an explicit disposition for each: CLAIMABLE, ACTIVE_CLAIM, TERMINAL_RETURN, DUPLICATE_DERIVED, AUTHORITY_BLOCKED or INVALID.
The receipt records exact evidence paths and source head/epoch so a fresh worker can prove why it selected a portfolio job or crossed into discovery.
Missing derived root is treated as empty-with-evidence, not as an inferred error or as proof that compounding exists.
Terminal outcomes block replay; expired/non-expired claims are distinguished using the contract semantics rather than directory existence alone.
Two workers evaluating the same snapshot produce the same ordered dispositions; claiming remains atomic create-if-absent and is not replaced by the receipt.
A canary fixture covering terminal Live + nine active seed claims + no derived root proves DISCOVERY_ALLOWED without human routing.

dedup_note: Repository search found no existing proposal for a portfolio allocator skip-reason/selection receipt. This does not replace the role-fluid allocator, portfolio job claims, Live projection, or autonomous G2->G3 work; it instruments the newly introduced portfolio fallback boundary so selection and fallback are independently auditable.
